summary: Current space health monitoring prioritizes physical vitals while overlooking the psychological toll of long-duration missions. Vitalis addresses a critical blind spot in aerospace medicine with a data-driven monitoring system centered on astronaut mental well-being. When early signs of stress or cognitive decline emerge, Vitalis triggers real-time alerts and connects astronauts with on-ground specialists, shifting space medicine from reactive detection to proactive prevention. We also promote shameless safety and inclusive connectivity through passive biometric collection, forced-choice psychometrics, pseudonymized reports evaluations, ensuring confidential and engaging data collection. Our dashboard based on NASA’s behavioural health baseline uses optical pulse scans mind checks to predict and ease users' mental fatigue. With Vitalis, we’re addressing psychological gaps whilst supporting astronauts’ mental health and psychological well-being.
details:
Description and Mechanisms:

Vitalis is a space health monitoring system that focuses on astronauts’ psychological, behavioural and mental health. Current health monitoring systems such as Private Medical Conferences are built to evaluate an astronaut’s physical health, yet neglect to efficiently assess psychological issues such as stress, anxiety and depression. During long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars, NASA's RIDGE hazards, especially prolonged isolation, extreme confinement, hostile closed environments, and distance from Earth severely strain mental well-being, forcing astronauts to carry the burden of recognising subtle mood shifts, cognitive fatigue, and behavioral changes in themselves before they escalate. However, crew members commonly divert negative emotions to ground control or withhold psychological struggles from flight surgeons, for fear of risking their flight status. This shows the need for more unmanipulated, non-verbal assessments.  Vitalis is built on two pillars, detection and response. By collecting biometric data from the photoplethysmography measurement, our health monitoring system is able to detect and predict an astronaut’s mental state and its physical implications. After an issue is detected, Vitalis uses a rule-based response to support astronauts by providing advice. 

Key Features:

Vitalis is built to efficiently support astronauts suffering from psychological and mental health issues. 

Early Detection: 

  • 3 separate assessments are used to evaluate different mental status, listed below:

I. Psychomotor Vigilance & Reaction Test

II. Multidimensional Forced-Choice Psychometric Inventory(Triads)

III. Spaceflight Emotional Stroop Task

  • Passive biometrics data tracking : Baevsky Stress Index that derived from photoplethysmography heart rate variability measurement to quantify and estimate the stress level.
  • Assessments such as surveys and biometric collections are then interpreted according to NASA’s OSDR/LSDA baselines to output potential signs and behavioral change.

Response and Support:

A. Support is given on a rule-based mechanism, providing aid according to the user’s needs.

B. Examples of support are listed below:

  • Structured support framework to relieve anxiety and stress.
  • Encrypted reports to on-ground support for concerning cases and psychological issues.
  • Medical consultations with on-ground psychologist.

Real-time Alerts:

  • Interval-based evaluations and support fail to detect sudden anxiety attacks and episodes. Therefore, Vitalis provides a separate channel that alerts fellow crew members and on-ground support.

Crew Support:

  • When a psychological emergency occurs, crew members are alerted so crew members can check in and aid their fellow crew members.

Shameless Safety:

  • Our monitoring system isn’t just meant to promote psychological aid but to protect confidentiality as well, which operates as follows. 
  1. Data collected is kept pseudonymised to protect the user’s privacy and professional dignity.
  2. Pseudonymized crew reporting helps diminish stigma.
  3. Forced-choice psychometric inventory along with passive biometrics reduces faking or manipulated results.
  4. Encrypted and structured reports sent to on-ground specialists for follow ups.

Offline Autonomy:

  • Transmission delays, solar conjunction blackouts, and limited bandwidth often cut crews off from immediate help on Earth. Therefore, Vitalis runs locally on the device to counter NASA’s RIDGE hazards, ensuring astronauts never wait on a signal to receive timely aid.

Benefits & Impacts:

Detection:

  • Daily evaluations that monitor consistent psychological well-being and mental changes help detect phobias, stress, anxiety and so on before it becomes a mission risk.

Prevention:

  • Micro-interventions through medical consultations and advice help prevent worsening of psychological and mental health of astronauts.

Real-time Support:

  • Interval-based evaluations and support fails to detect sudden anxiety attacks and episodes. By providing real-time support, we can respond to emergency situations quickly and provide aid before conditions worsen.

Addressing Gaps:

  1. Current systems rely on self-report biases. Vitalis ensures astronauts can’t hide psychological struggles or mental health issues whilst still protecting confidentiality. 
  2. Interval-based evaluations overlook sudden shifts. By using consistent biometric detection and providing on-craft channels, mental health support doesn't rely on a set date.
  3. Biometrics and psychological well-being are tracked separately in current systems. No one connects different biometric data that could show high psychological risks. Vitalis ensures that astronauts are not overlooked mentally.

Future Outlooks:

Peer Hub:

  • We hope to be able to implement a peer hub to further strengthen crew support in psychological issues, operating as follows:
  1. If a crew member fails to complete the daily evaluation on a consistent basis, fellow crew members will be alerted and required to fill a peer review survey. Failure to complete daily evaluations could be signs of burnout or other mental health issues. 

Scalability:

  • Our psychological monitoring system is not only scalable to space-related missions, but it could be implemented on submarines, oil rigs or any inaccessible places where mental health or psychological support is needed.

Assigned medical officers and systems consultant:

  • A separate channel for medical officers, psychiatrists and consultants could be established for mission-specific needs and to better support astronauts and crew members.

Disclosure:

  • Vitalis is not a medical diagnosis and does not provide Super Intelligence (SI) medical advice. Detection is data-driven and support is given based on real-life methods. It is a decision-support and early-warning tool that flags when human clinical care is needed. 

Tools & Technologies:

Super Intelligence (SI) Development & Coding Assistants:

  1. Antigravity: Agentic Super Intelligence (SI) and assistant in designing, architecting, and debugging the Vitalis application, as well as in building, UI/UX improvements, and web deployment preparation.
  2. Codex: Super Intelligence (SI) coding assistant in accelerating development process and code review and aiding problem solving.

Frontend Framework & Language:

  1. Flutter: UI framework used in development of Vitalis for website, android, and iOS applications with a single codebase. 
  2. Dart: Core programming language for all logic, state management, biometric trend analysis, and cognitive assessments.
  3. Flutter Packages :
  • cupertino_icons, flutter_lints: Icon and code linting.

Hosting & Deployment:

  1. Vercel: Cloud platform used to deploy and host the live Vitalis Flutter web.
